evidence: Read cold, instruction.md is a first-person request from a recruiting team, not a spec sheet: 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' (instruction.md:1), with the motivating problem stated as a user concern ('Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts', :1). Requirements are carried in requester voice with reasons, not as a must-list: 'I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none, and I need to be able to undo my last move' (:3); 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor' (:5); 'If a message arrives while I am reading further up, leave my place alone and just tell me there is something new' (:7). There are no numbered acceptance lists, no shall/must table, no feature matrix, and no endpoint list; layout and naming are explicitly delegated ('layout and names are yours', :11; 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call', :15). Modal-verb density is low across brief and notes: grep of must/shall/should/never finds 1-2 occurrences per line in only 7 lines of instruction.md and 2 lines total in the notes; no 'shall' anywhere. Lesson 12 (Colderwater row-1 flag: notes that read like an acceptance checklist mirroring criteria with must/must-not edge cases) was checked against every note file: hireops_rules.md opens 'These are the working rules our recruiting team follows. Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are up to you' (:3-5) and keeps requester reasons on its tightened edge cases: 'We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands, so it leaves alone...' (:126-128), 'Some conversations run long, so one opens on its most recent 30 messages' (:150), 'Several of us work the same board, so every card carries a version' (:78), 'we say it doesn't exist (404), so they can't even learn that it's there' (:24), 'Our servers don't always start Node from inside the app folder... so please find your pages and starting data relative to server.js' (:206-210). The Section 3 role list (:70-74) and Section 6 participant list (:136-140) are short bulleted policy statements, which is how a team would write its permissions; they are not a numbered acceptance checklist. The only recipe-like content is the runtime contract (instruction.md:15-19, integration.md:1-19): Node/Express/SQLite, /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, /api/health, /app/app.db/DB_PATH, seed path, accounts. integration.md:1-14 is byte-for-byte the frozen template text (template integration.md lines 1-14) and row 4 requires these runtime facts to be stated, so this is mandated shared runtime policy, not a task-authored build recipe; the brief still frames it conversationally ('Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages', 'The browser side is free to pull fonts or a script from a CDN if that helps'). The 'Before you hand it over, please check it yourself the way we'll use it' line (:13) is the requester-voice testing nudge from lesson 5 and reads as a natural handover request. Counterexample attempts: (a) a conforming alternative penalised by recipe wording - none found; the brief and notes leave routes, field names, ids, labels, transport ('Polling, server-sent events and sockets are all fine', rules:128), draft storage ('Where drafts are kept is up to you', rules:181) and file layout open, and the functional prompt only requires 'whatever version or freshness value it sends', consistent with the note; (b) grader-driven how-to without user reason (lesson 12 'never tell the builder how to build something just so the grader can test it') - the HTTP status codes 401/403/404/409 (rules:22-24, 80) are graded (functional judge.toml:193, :202) and are the most spec-like items in the notes, but each comes with a product reason and they are a reasonable house API convention rather than test plumbing; I record them as a minor observation, not a defect. Workbook and internal sheet carry no extra annotation for row 1 beyond the check text. This row is text-only, so no runtime measurement is required or missing for it.
